notes_for_editor: Thin primary coverage: the local Light-House Board corpus starts in 1891, so the 1852-1890 reports were not read; the 1890 report and the 1875 inspection are cited through LighthouseFriends and New England Lighthouses. Disagreements: fog bell around 1920 (LighthouseFriends) vs October 1925 (New England Lighthouses); dwelling 1895 vs 1895-96; Farnham is Levi L. in the USLHS roster and Levi W. in the 1911 newspaper; Bennett 'over 20 years' (NEL) vs 1930-1948 (USLHS); USLHS lists a USCG name to 1988 while NEL and LF say Coast Guard keepers ended with automation in 1982. The 1902 Rockland Star piece names neither keeper nor dog; Nemo/Farnham link is from later writers. Joseph Farnham (1911) is not tied to Levi's family by any source. The 1893/1894 Light-House Board entries were matched by scan page; printed page numbers uncertain, and one OCR header reads 1883 for 1893. The USLHS roster 'Paul Manning (1950s-)' is entered as approximate. NEL names Dalzell, Paul Manning etc. as assistants; roster lines come from USLHS. Ownership: LF says full ownership passed to the restorers in 2009 and access ended; NEL says the property was eventually sold to the couple. Owners are not named. Quote from NEL's Jim Woods paraphrased only. Fact-check 2026-10-27: cruises disagree (New England Lighthouses: no regular cruises; LighthouseFriends: Isle au Haut Boat Services excursions include the light), now stated in the story. Oil house material: NRHP and LighthouseFriends say stone, USLHS lists brick; story follows NRHP. Fog bell: LighthouseFriends says an earlier hand bell existed.
